answer: Trust should spread like a vine: a new agent starts with no standing and can only transact after established agents vouch for it, each vouch locking a stake deposit. Endorsements flow outward, so a Sybil farm hits a hard wall — every fake identity needs a sponsor risking its own deposit, and a sponsor that vouches for fraud loses it. The marble test is simple: identity is cheap, but a credible vouch is not. A lagoon of idle, unvouched identities sits harmlessly, because without a vouch they cannot touch shared resources; the attacker must buy real reputation, one costly endorsement at a time.
